# Ezekiel 12 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Again the LORD's message came to me:

**2** "Son of man, you're living among rebels — people who have eyes but refuse to see, who have ears but refuse to hear. They're completely rebellious.

**3** So pack your bags for exile, son of man. Do it during the day where everyone can watch. Move your belongings from where you live to somewhere else while they watch. Maybe they'll get the message — even though they're rebels.

**4** Bring out your packed bags during the day where they can see. Then at evening, leave — the way people leave when they're going into exile, while they watch.

**5** While they watch, dig a hole through the wall and carry your bags out through it.

**6** Hoist your bags on your shoulder at dusk where they can see, and cover your face so you can't see the ground. I am making you a living sign for the people of Israel."

**7** So I did exactly as I was told. During the day, I packed my bags like an exile. In the evening, I dug through the wall with my bare hands. At dusk, I hoisted my bags on my shoulder and carried them out while everyone watched.

**8** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**9** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**10** Tell them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: This message is about the prince in Jerusalem and all the Israelites living there.'

**11** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**12** Their prince will carry his belongings on his shoulder at dusk and leave through a hole dug in the wall. He will cover his face so he can't see the ground.

**13** But I will spread My net and catch him in My trap. I will bring him to Babylon in the land of the Chaldeans — but he will never see it. He will die there.

**14** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**15** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**16** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**17** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**18** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**19** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**20** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**21** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**22** "Son of man, what's this saying people keep repeating in Israel? 'Time keeps passing and none of these prophecies come true.'

**23** Tell them, 'The Lord GOD says: I'm putting an end to that cynical saying. No one in Israel will repeat it again.' Instead say, 'The time is at hand! Every prophecy is about to be fulfilled!'

**24** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**25** I am the LORD, and when I speak, it happens. There will be no more delays. In your own lifetime, you rebellious people, I will say it and do it, declares the Lord GOD."

**26** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**27** And the LORD's word about the exile and its certainty pressed upon the rebellious people of Israel as a warning for the present hour.

**28** So tell them, 'The Lord GOD says: No more delays! Whatever I say will happen — and soon!' declares the Lord GOD."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **12:3-7**: Ezekiel becomes a one-man drama — packing bags, digging through walls at night, covering his face. The exiles watch in real time. It's performance art with a devastating punchline: this is your king's future.

- **12:13**: The creepiest detail: Zedekiah will go to Babylon but never see it. Years later, he was literally blinded before being shipped there. The prophecy was more accurate than anyone imagined.

- **12:22**: The people's attitude is timeless: 'These prophecies never come true.' Delayed judgment feels like no judgment. But God's patience is not God's permission.

— PNEUMA
